text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- More than 1,000 road tankers discharge petrol in Lagos area over the weekend in a bid to end crippling fuel shortage.
- Afrobeat musician Fela Anikulapo-Kuti sues drug enforcement agency for 100 million naira over his arrest for alleged possession of cannabis.
- Volume of trade on Nigerian stock exchange drops sharply as traders observe rather than trade with newly installed computerised clearing system.

- Shell oil company lost a total of 800,000 barrels of oil when production was shut down for one week last month in Nembe over communal disturbances, says the company's community liaison officer Aderemi Oni.
- Nigeria railways confirms two people died when a train derailed near Lagos on Saturday night.

- Military ruler General Sani Abacha, in a message to an air force conference in Kaduna, northern Nigeria, restates his commitment to hand over power to a democratically elected civilian president next year.
- Federal government begins payment of cash calls, funds due to oil companies in their joint venture operations with Nigeria.
